ideas.title: The 47-Minute Rule
ideas.concept: A data-driven post revealing that the average business owner wastes 47 minutes per day on tasks Claude AI can do in 3 seconds. Visual would be a split-screen infographic showing common daily tasks (email drafts, meeting summaries, proposal writing) with time comparisons — human vs AI. Ends with a calculation: 47 mins x 250 workdays = 195 hours/year of your life you'll never get back.
ideas.hook: You're not busy. You're just doing $12/hour work in a $200/hour seat.

ideas.title: What Broke When I Tried To DIY My Automations
ideas.concept: A story-format post walking through a real (or composite) client scenario where they tried duct-taping Zapier, spreadsheets, and ChatGPT together before coming to Accelod. Visual would be a messy whiteboard-style diagram of their tangled setup, next to the clean N8N + GoHighLevel + Claude stack that replaced it. Lesson: cheap automation is the most expensive kind.
ideas.hook: He spent 6 months and £4,200 building an automation that broke every Tuesday.

ideas.title: GoHighLevel Isn't A CRM
ideas.concept: A tool breakdown / hot-take post reframing GoHighLevel as an operating system, not a CRM — and explaining the 4 layers most users never activate (pipelines that trigger workflows, workflows that call Claude, Claude that writes back into Google Workspace, all logged via N8N). Visual would be a stacked diagram showing the 4 layers with a bold label: 'You bought a Ferrari to drive to Tesco.'
ideas.hook: 90% of GoHighLevel users are paying £297/month to send emails. That's insane.

ig_caption:
He spent 6 months and £4,200 building an automation that broke every Tuesday. 🧨

His setup? Zapier stacked on spreadsheets, glued together with ChatGPT prompts and prayer.

Every Tuesday, a Zap timed out. Leads vanished. Invoices duplicated. His VA spent hours cleaning up the mess.

We rebuilt it in 9 days: N8N running the logic, GoHighLevel handling the CRM, Claude doing the thinking.

Zero breakages in 4 months. He got his Tuesdays back.

Cheap automation isn't cheap. It's the most expensive tax you'll ever pay.

Sound familiar? 👇
